config.goal: Port adam.cu (HeCBench adam-cuda; grid-stride Adam optimizer, 10 updates per parameter) to idiomatic SYCL 2020 with zero dpct helpers; the float32 parameters must match the C++ reference within atol 1e-5 + rtol 1e-4. Tolerance: 1 - 0.999^t cancels, so a 1-ulp difference in pow (GPU vs CPU libm) becomes a ~6e-5 relative difference in the bias-corrected v. Where v starts near 0 the update m/sqrt(v) is large and p moves by up to ~3 (min p is -2.02), so the error scales with |p|: simulating a 1-ulp pow change gives 3.15e-5 at that element and 8.5e-7 at the 99.99th percentile. The bound is then 6.7x above the worst case and over 10x above the rest, while an indexing, mode or update-order bug moves p by 1e-3 or more.

input.summary: Ported adam.cu to SYCL 2020 in migrated/adam_sycl.cpp. It compiles with icpx -fsycl with zero diagnostics and with add_dpct_include=false, so no dpct headers are needed. The file has no dpct:: calls, DPCT_* macros or <dpct/...> includes. Changes from the SYCLomatic output: the kernel is a plain 1-D grid-stride loop inside an sycl::nd_range<1> parallel_for, using sycl::malloc_device/sycl::free, q.memcpy, sycl::pow and sycl::sqrt, and an in-order queue. The per-element Adam arithmetic and the time_step loop are unchanged. adam_input.hpp and reference.h were already dpct-free. Not verified: I have no tool that runs the binary, so the output has not been compared to the reference within atol 1e-5 / rtol 1e-4. The main numerical risk is pow: sycl::pow on the device may differ from CPU powf by about 1 ulp, which the task notes put well within tolerance.
